findings.title: Registry PDF 预览用 blob+iframe，触发顶层导航 about:blank 并丢失登录态
findings.detail: file-preview-dialog.tsx 第 184–211 行在 kind==='pdf' 时 fetch contentUrl 生成 blob URL，再由 file-preview-content.tsx 第 80–83 行放进 <iframe src={url}>。该写法在 Chrome 下会劫持顶层页面导航，导致当前标签页变成 about:blank，随后访问业务路由被重定向到 /main/login。第 3、4、5 轮 QA 连续复现同一现象。
findings.impact: 任务明确要求 PDF 在应用内预览；默认 Registry 路径直接不可用，且会破坏整个会话，属于最严重的框架级附件缺陷。
findings.suggestedChange: Registry 默认 PDF 预览改用 pdfjs-dist 渲染到 canvas（或使用不会改变顶层导航的嵌入方式），不要用 fetch+blob+iframe；同时在 SKILL 增加 PDF 的会话保持自检项。

findings.title: file SKILL 把“PDF via a fetched blob”写成推荐实现，且验证清单遗漏 PDF
findings.detail: SKILL 第 233 行明确写“Preview supports ... PDF via a fetched blob”，与 Registry 中引发缺陷的实现一致；第 245 行的预览集成验证清单只要求验证 DOCX/XLSX/PPTX 与请求生命周期，完全没有要求验证 PDF。
findings.impact: Agent 会照着 skill 复现已损坏的 PDF 实现，并且自检时不会覆盖 PDF，导致缺陷跨越 3 个验证轮次。
findings.suggestedChange: 修正 skill 的 PDF 描述为 canvas/安全嵌入方案，并在验证清单与示例中加入 PDF 的会话保持与 about:blank 回归检查。
findings.claimed: skill 第 233 行称 PDF 通过 fetched blob 提供受支持预览。
findings.observed: 该 blob+iframe 路径正是第 3–5 轮 about:blank+掉登录态的根因，skill 未提示任何风险。

processNotes.author: implementer
processNotes.summary: Repaired the equipment after-sales service and inspection application. Duplicate equipment codes now return a 409 business conflict instead of a raw SQLite unique-index error, and customer/equipment/ticket selects render names rather than raw ids. The ticket workflow captures handling hours in the completion dialog, return puts a ticket back in progress instead of the assignment queue, system-generated records no longer store untranslated English content, and manual ticket submission records a visible intake trace (register, route, notify). Notification titles are stored as translation keys and rendered in the recipient's language, and messages can be deleted. Ticket attachments are no longer enumerable by a user without access to the ticket, uploads are validated by extension and magic bytes, and attachment content URLs carry the application base path so preview and download work. A second verification round fixed four observed business defects: PDF and XLSX attachment previews (an octet-stream PDF Blob was retyped for the browser viewer, and a valid workbook missing the optional xl/styles.xml part is normalized before the OOXML viewer), an authorization leak that let a read-only observer read handling hours and the closure summary and call the return action, the messages inbox now refetching on reconnect, and server business errors rendered in the request's language (Chinese) instead of English. A third verification round addressed two more observed defects: the PDF attachment preview could navigate the tab to about:blank (the PDF branch began validating %PDF- magic bytes and retyping the Blob), and the XLSX viewer's hardcoded English zoom and tab controls are now localized to the interface language. The PDF fix was insufficient: the running build already contained it and the tab still left the application. A fourth round removed the browser's PDF viewer from the flow entirely. Because that viewer, handed a blob: document in a frame, could claim the top-level navigation and leave the tab on about:blank, the preview now validates the %PDF- magic bytes and renders the pages itself onto canvases with pdf.js, so the document never leaves the dialog.

blockers.title: Cookie-authenticated API writes fail with INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN in standards test harness
blockers.symptom: POST requests authenticated by a session cookie (for example POST /api/service/tickets/:id/submit and POST /api/service/integrations/keys) returned 403 {"code":"INVALID_CSRF_ORIGIN"} while the same GET requests and the Better Auth sign-in POST succeeded.
blockers.rootCause: auth.required() calls checkCookieWriteOrigin(), which rejects a cookie-bearing write unless its Origin/Referer is a Better Auth trusted origin. Those origins derive from the authentication provider's baseURL, which it reads from the app config value app.publicOrigin. In the test harness that value was never set, so the trusted-origin set was empty. The tests had also passed a publicOrigin option to createInstalledStandaloneServer, but that option is not part of StandaloneServerOptions and was silently ignored.
blockers.resolution: Set env APP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN (the documented env of server/config/app.ts publicOrigin) on the installed test server and send a matching Origin: http://localhost header on every cookie-authenticated write in tests/logic/app-server.test.ts. All four service operations API tests then pass.

blockers.title: PDF attachment stored as application/octet-stream previews as an empty frame
blockers.symptom: Opening a PDF attachment whose upload carried no media type (stored and served as application/octet-stream) showed an empty preview frame instead of the document, while a PDF stored as application/pdf previewed normally in the same ticket.
blockers.rootCause: The client fetched the content URL into a Blob and kept the response Content-Type (application/octet-stream), then passed that Blob to URL.createObjectURL. The browser built-in PDF viewer renders only a blob whose type is application/pdf, so it produced a blank frame. The attachment content route echoes the stored media type, and an upload without a media type is stored as application/octet-stream.
blockers.resolution: The file-component extension PDF preview branch now retypes the fetched Blob to application/pdf before creating the object URL unless it is already application/pdf (client/extensions/nocobase-file-component-ui/components/file-preview-dialog.tsx). Verified with Playwright against a rebuilt app: the octet-stream PDF now yields a blob: iframe whose document Chrome renders, and a component test asserts the created Blob type is application/pdf.

blockers.title: XLSX preview refuses a valid workbook that omits the optional xl/styles.xml part
blockers.symptom: A minimal xlsx fixture (a valid OOXML workbook that Excel opens) failed with 'Unable to render this Office Open XML file.', while a workbook written by a full generator previewed normally.
blockers.rootCause: @silurus/ooxml's XlsxViewer requires the xl/styles.xml part. ECMA-376 leaves that part optional, so a hand-built workbook that omits it is refused even though its content is intact. Reproduced by generating a minimal xlsx with only the required parts (it failed) and by adding an xl/styles.xml that was neither declared in [Content_Types].xml nor referenced from the workbook relationships (it rendered), proving the part's mere presence is the gate rather than its content or declarations.
blockers.resolution: The OOXML preview now checks for xl/styles.xml with a filtered unzip before handing an xlsx to the viewer and, only when the part is absent, adds a minimal styles part and re-zips the archive (fflate added as a client devDependency); a workbook that already has the part is passed through byte-for-byte. Verified with Playwright against a rebuilt app: the previously failing fixture now renders a canvas with no error, and component tests cover both the injected and the pass-through case.

blockers.title: Read-only observer could read internal handling fields and invoke the return action
blockers.symptom: A service observer (no viewInternal, no return capability) saw 'Hours spent' and the closure/handling summary on a ticket, received the handling summary from GET /tickets/:id/records, and a direct POST /tickets/:id/return answered 200.
blockers.rootCause: listRecords only nulled content for a record kind 'internal', a kind no transition writes; the handling summary and hours are stored on the 'handle' record and were returned unchanged. toTicketView exposed closeSummary unconditionally, and returnTicket performed no capability check, so the state change relied only on the UI hiding it.
blockers.resolution: listRecords now resolves canViewInternal once and hides content for the handle/internal record kinds and nulls hours for a reader without viewInternal, so both the ticket view and the direct records route obey it; toTicketView hides closeSummary unless internalVisible; returnTicket begins with access.require(tickets, 'return'). A new app-server test asserts the observer receives null hours, null handling content and null closeSummary and a 403 when calling return.

blockers.title: Messages inbox never refetches when the browser comes back online
blockers.symptom: A message written while the browser was offline (or the tab was hidden) did not appear until a manual reload; the inbox never refetched on reconnect.
blockers.rootCause: The inbox loaded once through useAsyncData and registered no listener for connection or visibility recovery, so nothing re-ran the fetch after the browser regained connectivity.
blockers.resolution: client/pages/service/messages.tsx registers window 'online' and document 'visibilitychange' (when visible) listeners that reload the inbox, removing them on unmount and re-binding when the loader identity changes. Verified with Playwright against a rebuilt app: dispatching an online event produced a second GET /notifications/in-app.

blockers.title: Server business errors stayed English in a Chinese interface
blockers.symptom: Domain errors surfaced as English sentences inside a Chinese UI, for example '保存失败 The equipment code EQ-QA-B02-01 already exists.' and '附件上传失败。 Unsupported file type: .exe'.
blockers.rootCause: Server error messages were plain English strings with no translation lookup; the client renders error.message directly, and the application server locale files existed but were empty, so even a correct lookup would have found no resource.
blockers.resolution: DomainError now carries an optional key and params; server/routes/helpers.ts translates the key (defaulting to the English message) through getRequestTranslator with literal-key separators and uses it in the {error, code} body, and the integration content route uses the same serializer. server/locales/en-US.ts and zh-CN.ts map all 70 messages, with explicit key+params at the six sites that interpolate a value. Verified with a zh-CN request returning 设备编码 … 已存在。 beside the unchanged CONFLICT code, and an en-US request returning the English sentence.

blockers.title: PDF attachment preview navigated the tab to about:blank instead of rendering
blockers.symptom: In the ticket attachment preview, moving to the PDF file lost the ticket page: the tab ended at about:blank and the next visit to /main/service/tickets/:id redirected to /main/login. The other formats (PNG, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX) previewed in place, and upload/download and corrupt-file handling otherwise passed.
blockers.rootCause: The client handed the document to Chrome's built-in PDF viewer as a blob: URL inside an iframe. In the acceptance engine that viewer, given a blob document in a frame, could take over the top-level navigation: the tab left the application for about:blank and the page was torn down, after which the in-memory session was gone and the next visit to /main/service/tickets/:id redirected to /main/login. The application log confirmed the content route answered 200 with the correct 593-byte PDF immediately before the navigation, so the fetch, the response headers and the stored media type were not at fault, and the earlier %PDF- byte-retyping fix was already present in the running build. A bare about:blank navigation does not by itself end the session (navigating a fresh session to about:blank and back preserved it), so the logout was a consequence of the tab or renderer teardown, not of the preview request. Sandboxing the iframe was rejected because this engine renders no PDF inside a sandboxed frame, which blanked the preview.
blockers.resolution: The PDF preview no longer uses the browser plugin or a blob: URL. A new client/extensions/nocobase-file-component-ui/components/previewers/pdf-preview.tsx fetches the bytes with the same origin-aware credentials, validates them with the %PDF- magic-byte check (isPdfContent) before any viewer is created, then loads them with pdfjs-dist (imported dynamically; its worker is emitted by Vite as an asset and resolved through the runtime base path) and draws each page onto a canvas inside the dialog, capped at 30 pages with a localized notice (files.pdfPageLimit). PreviewBody in file-preview-dialog.tsx no longer creates an object URL, and FilePreviewContent's pdf branch no longer renders an iframe. pdfjs-dist 5.6.205 was added as a client devDependency. Verified against the rebuilt application with a fresh browser session signed in through the UI: clicking Preview: sample.pdf, and reaching sample.pdf through the preview dialog's Next file, kept the top URL on /main/service/tickets/6, created no iframe, fetched the emitted pdf.worker asset, rendered a canvas whose pixel analysis shows the document text, kept the session valid across a reload, and produced no console error; PNG, DOCX, XLSX and PPTX previews still render. Unit tests assert the canvas rendering, that no object URL or iframe is created, the non-PDF rejection, and the page-cap notice.

blockers.title: XLSX preview controls stayed in English in a Chinese interface
blockers.symptom: With the interface in Chinese, the XLSX viewer's zoom and tab-scroll buttons still exposed English accessible names and title tooltips (Zoom out, Zoom in, Zoom, Scroll tabs left, Scroll tabs right), and the spreadsheet region label stayed English.
blockers.rootCause: @silurus/ooxml renders its spreadsheet chrome with hardcoded English strings and exposes no locale or labels option, so those strings never pass through the application's i18n; the file plugin's namespace does not translate them either.
blockers.resolution: After the viewer loads, the preview localizes its DOM in place (client/extensions/nocobase-file-component-ui/lib/xlsx-localization.ts): it sets title and aria-label on the tab-nav buttons and the zoom slider group, and the region label, using useTranslation('@nocobase/app-plugin-file') so the wording resolves through the application fallback namespace, and watches the viewer with a MutationObserver so controls created later are localized too. Keys files.xlsxZoom / xlsxZoomIn / xlsxZoomOut / xlsxScrollTabsLeft / xlsxScrollTabsRight / xlsxViewport were added to client/locales/en-US.ts and zh-CN.ts. Verified in a rebuilt app in a Chinese session: the controls read 缩小, 缩放, 放大, 向左滚动工作表标签, 向右滚动工作表标签 and the Chinese region label in both aria-label and title, while the English session still shows English.

improvements.title: Standalone test-harness publicOrigin option is silently ignored
improvements.detail: tests/logic/app-server.test.ts declares a publicOrigin option on its test server options and forwards it to createStandaloneServer, but the underlying StandaloneServerOptions/CreateStandaloneScopeOptions do not define publicOrigin, so it never reaches app config. The only working way to set the application public origin for an installed server is the APP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN environment override, which is non-obvious and makes cookie-write CSRF checks fail with a 403 that does not point at the missing origin.
improvements.suggestedChange: Either honour a publicOrigin option in the standalone server options, or have the test harness write app.publicOrigin into the runtime test config (or reject the unknown option) so a cookie-authenticated write test does not need to know about the APP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN indirection.

improvements.title: In-app notification items have no locale, so a server-produced title cannot be translated at write time
improvements.detail: The in-app notification table stores a single title per recipient with no locale column, and the i18n plugin keeps the active locale only in the session. A notification produced by a server service therefore cannot be written in the recipient's language. The workaround stores the stable translation key (for example service.notifications.needsAssignment) as the title and translates it in the client at read time, which leaves any already-persisted human-readable title untranslated.
improvements.suggestedChange: Let a notification be produced from a translation key plus arguments and resolve it against the recipient's locale at read time (or store the recipient locale with the item), so services never have to encode the localization convention in their title strings.

improvements.title: Base UI Select silently renders the raw value when Root has no items map
improvements.detail: The application's Select wraps @base-ui/react/select, whose Value renders the raw selected value unless Root receives an items prop that maps values to labels. A Select composed with only SelectItem children therefore shows an id or code instead of the label, with no warning at build or runtime. This is how customer and equipment filters displayed raw ids.
improvements.suggestedChange: Document the items requirement for Base UI Select in the UI workflow reference, or add a development warning when a Select has SelectItem children but no items map, so the missing labels surface before review.

improvements.title: File preview relies on the browser's built-in PDF viewer for attachments
improvements.detail: The file-component registry item previews a PDF by embedding the browser's PDF viewer in an iframe over a blob: URL. In the acceptance engine that viewer, given a blob document in a frame, could claim the top-level navigation and leave the application on about:blank, tearing down the page; the application has no way to detect or prevent it, and sandboxing the frame is not a fix because the engine renders no PDF inside a sandboxed frame. The shipped component also had no test that exercised a real PDF, so the failure was invisible until an upload.
improvements.suggestedChange: Render PDF pages without the browser plugin — for example by shipping a canvas-based viewer (pdf.js) as the default PDF preview — or at least document the plugin dependency and constrain the frame so a viewer failure cannot escape the page; add a fixture test that opens a real PDF.

improvements.title: @silurus/ooxml rejects a workbook missing the optional xl/styles.xml part
improvements.detail: The XLSX viewer treats the styles part as required, while ECMA-376 marks it optional and the part is absent from many minimally generated workbooks that Excel opens. The failure is reported only as the generic "Unable to render this Office Open XML file.", so the missing part is not discoverable from the error.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have the viewer tolerate a missing styles part (or accept a default styles sheet), or include the missing part name and stage in the error so an application can repair the file. A conformance fixture without xl/styles.xml belongs in the package tests.

improvements.title: Business domain errors have no built-in translation path
improvements.detail: Server services throw DomainError subclasses whose message is a user-visible English sentence. The route serializer emitted that message verbatim, and the application server locale files were empty templates, so a translated UI still showed English business errors and the only fix was to add key/params plumbing and hand-map every message.
improvements.suggestedChange: Give the domain-error base class an optional i18n key and arguments by default, translate in the shared response serializer, and ship the application server locale scaffolding with a documented convention (or a check that every thrown business message has a locale entry) so localization does not require each application to build the mechanism.

improvements.title: Declared capabilities and endpoint guards can drift without a failing test
improvements.detail: A permission set declares actions such as tickets.return, but enforcement lives in a separate access.require call inside each service function; one transition (returnTicket) omitted it, so an observer could call the endpoint even though the role never had the capability. Nothing tied the declared capability list to the endpoints that should enforce it.
improvements.suggestedChange: Derive or test endpoint guards from the declared capability set, so adding a capability or a transition without its access.require fails a test instead of silently expanding access; a matrix test that calls each mutating route as a role lacking its capability and expects 403 would catch this class.

improvements.title: Bundled XLSX viewer hardcodes English chrome with no localization option
improvements.detail: @silurus/ooxml's XlsxViewerOptions exposes imageResources, cellScale, resizable, showScrollbars, the zoom range and callbacks, but no locale, labels or messages option. Its zoom and tab-scroll controls and its spreadsheet region label are literal English strings, so an application cannot translate them through the shared i18n runtime and has to mutate the viewer's DOM after load.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a labels/locale option (or accept translated strings) to XlsxViewerOptions so the chrome and the region label come from the application's translator instead of being hardcoded.

2. Declare reusable collection permissions with `defineDatabasePermission`; compose user-facing business operations as composite resources with `defineCompositeResource` from `@nocobase/authorization/core`. Explicitly name fields, relation capabilities and every collection a workflow touches.
3. In the owning provider's `boot`, opt collections in with `authz.database.collections.add`, register composites with `authz.compositeResources.define`, record access with `authz.recordAccess.define` and settings items with `authz.settings.add`. Then add a workspace subsection with `authz.ui.sections.add({ name, title, parent })` and list each composite or settings item in it with `authz.ui.place(reference, { section, group? })` (the permission workspace lists sections and subsections on the left and the selected subsection's resources, under optional `authz.ui.groups`, on the right; an unplaced composite or settings item goes under its default section's Other with a startup warning, and a misplaced one fails a development start). Pages are not registered on the server: the client route tree lists them. Release subject registrations at shutdown.

evidence.observation: SKILL 明确未注册 collection 默认拒绝、catalog 与 record 类型差异，以及 can/require/authorize 的使用边界。
evidence.excerpt:
- `settings`, `composite` and `database.collection` are catalog types: a check on an unregistered item or action is denied with `RESOURCE_ACTION_NOT_SUPPORTED`. `page`, `user`, `notification` and Hub types are record types that declare actions only; their grants use `id: '*'` for every record.
- A composite action composes exactly the grants it lists, never another composite. A data scope targets the one collection its grant actions name, whose type must declare `recordAccess` (`database.collection` does). Grant page access separately; a page grant never authorizes a server endpoint.
- `can` is for feature visibility. `require` needs an unconditional permit and rejects conditional decisions. Business endpoints use `authorize`, reject denial or missing policies, and consume `conditions.database` without resolving collection grants again.
